Phin Pia是一種泰國傳統弦樂器，音色清亮透徹，具有獨特的金屬質感。其音域跨: The phin pia is a traditional Thai string instrument with a clear, transparent timbre and a distinctive metallic quality. Its range is fairly wide and it can produce several layers of sound, from low to bright. It sounds by plucking or striking the strings, which gives a bright, carrying tone with a slight nasal quality. The resonating body strengthens the overtones, so the timbre keeps its warmth and stays clearly expressive. Compared with the soft, heavy guzheng it is lighter and more agile; compared with the harp its timbre is more Southeast Asian, with a distinctive harmony, and it suits the melodies of traditional folk music.

The phin pia is a traditional plucked instrument from Thailand and Laos, classed as a keyboard chordophone. It is trapezoid or boat-shaped, with several metal strings, and sounds by plucking or striking them. The timbre is clear and transparent, with a distinctive metallic quality and a slight nasal edge. Compared with the guzheng it is lighter and more agile, with a wide range; it keeps the Southeast Asian character and carries well. It is widely used in court music, temple ritual and folk festivals, and is an important instrument of traditional Southeast Asian music.

This plucked instrument has a long history in the region, going back to the ancient folk-music traditions of Southeast Asia. Its distinctive construction reflects the skill of local makers and their deep understanding of music.
